en: *Svapnādhyāya*, possibly by Vibhūticandra;
translated by Vibhūticandra, Tohoku No. 1749.

Diplomatically transcribed, edited, and reproduced by Saerji, “The Sanskrit Manuscript of the *Svapnādhyāya* Preserved in Tibet. In: Ernst Steinkellner et al. (eds.), *Sanskrit Manuscripts in China*. Beijing 2009. pp. 241–257.
(cf. MBB-II-67)
Homage to the Buddha.
I shall proclaim the chapter on dreams composed by Bṛhaspati, by which the auspicious and inauspicious [results] for men are known within their dreams. (1)
A dream in the first watch yields its fruit within a year;
in the second, within eight months; and in the third, within three months.
But by four [repetitions], the fruit shall be firmly secured for men in the fourth [case];
at the time of dawn, the fruit shall be attained within ten days. (3)
The blow of weapons, a body filled with worms, being cast from the battlefield, the cleansing of the limbs,
the smearing of excrement, and the flow of blood.
And in dreams, approaching women who should not be approached is [an omen of] grain. 4.
Mounting bulls, elephants, palaces, mountain peaks, and trees,
and having boarded a boat or taken up a lute—
After eating and weeping, there will certainly be the acquisition of wealth. || 5 ||
But he who sees at the end of a dream a king, an elephant, a horse,
gold, a bull, or a cow, his household increases.
If one grows alone upon a tree that bears both milk and fruit,
and while situated there one becomes aware [of it], one shall quickly obtain wealth.
But he who, having eaten while staying in a palace, drinks water at the edge of the ocean—
even if born in the family of a slave— he too shall become a king.
Whoever sees a lamp, food, fruit, a flower, a maiden, an umbrella, a chariot,
or a banner at the end of a dream, certainly obtains those very things.
Furthermore, he who eats human flesh in a dream gains five hundred [coins] for each foot and one thousand for eating an arm. (10)
The gain from eating [the head] is a thousandfold; one of meritorious body obtains a kingdom, or perhaps a man is born as a lord of many crores. 11.
He who encircles his house or cities with weapons shall obtain a kingdom within his house or become a sovereign in the city. (12)
He who, having obtained a pair of sandals and an umbrella,
perceives a stainless and sharp sword, possesses fortune that faces in every direction.
One who has embarked on a boat may meet with disaster, yet he shall also emerge from it;
one should predict his journey abroad as well as his swift return. 14.
He who, at the end of a dream, mounts a donkey, a camel, or a horse known to him,
even while remaining there, awakens and attains sovereign power.
He whose teeth fall out and then grow back again, or fall out repeatedly, will suffer the loss of kinsmen and his offspring shall perish. (16)
If he is anointed with oil, fat, and ghee,
one should diagnose him as having a disease.
If a spirit wearing red garments leads him toward the southern direction, [one should likewise diagnose his condition].
Taking hold of the hand of a dark-skinned woman, one should predict his death. || 18 ||
For that man who embraces in a dream a woman wearing red garments and anointed with red perfumes, this night is his last. (19)
He who embraces in a dream a woman wearing white garments and anointed with white perfumes shall possess prosperity in every direction.
If anyone, while asleep at night, is bitten by leeches, a daughter will be born to him; there is no need for further deliberation on this matter. 21.
If one is pursued in a dream by horned or tusked beasts,
or by a monkey or a boar, there will be danger from the royal family. (22)
If one sees the solar disc or the moon in a dream, he obtains a treasury from men, or they bestow a house upon him. (23)
He who is bound with fetters or again by the noose of the arms— either a son is born to him, or his very stability shall be pointed out as lost.
He who is bitten on the right arm even by a scorched snake,
or by a white snake, shall obtain a thousandfold gain on the completion of the tenth day. 25.
He who drinks blood or even liquor in a dream—such a Brāhmaṇa obtains knowledge, while another obtains wealth. || 26 ||
He who drinks milk mixed with foam from a milch cow in a dream has partaken of the soma sacrifice; one should predict for him other prosperity as well.
By giving curd, there will be joy; by wheat, the arrival of wealth;
one should know that through barley comes the attainment of sacrifice, and through white mustard seeds, gain as well.

When [the enemy] is in flower, one should cause [one's own] work to flower; when he has borne fruit, one should achieve the highest growth. When he is smoking, one should smoke; and when he is blazing, one should bring about wealth.
Whether on a seat, or in a bed, or in his body, or in a vehicle, or in a house,
when it blazes forth, his prosperity shall be manifest in every direction.
He is freed from disease, free from affliction... [the text breaks off; approximately four more verses in Tibetan follow].
